To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patient empowerment is a valued outcome, even if it does not bring about health status benefits, and that research is needed to tighten up the construct and develop a generic measure to enable evaluation of healthcare services on this basis.
patient empowerment can and should be considered as a patient-reported outcome for healthcare evaluation, but that research is required before it is possible to do this.

patient empowerment is a valued outcome of healthcare even when patients do not gain in health status; that it is important to consider patient empowerment itself as an outcome of healthcare, and to develop an appropriate patient reported measure of empowerment; that research is needed to (re)develop an appropriate and widely-applicable generic measure of patient-reported empowerment; and that research is needed on how people trade-off empowerment and gain in other health outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of patient-centred healthcare evaluation, which can be used to inform the development and implementation of patient empowerment strategies.
the development of a generic patient empowerment measure to facilitate comparative evaluations of healthcare on the basis of this outcome.
understanding how people experience and value empowerment, and the implications for healthcare evaluation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
patient empowerment is a valued outcome from healthcare and is worthy of consideration as a measurable patient reported outcome.
patient empowerment can and should be a valued patient outcome from healthcare.
the patient empowerment paradigm is an exciting new direction for healthcare evaluation, but it requires a great deal of research before it can be implemented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patient empowerment is a complex construct and that there is a need to understand the patient empowerment construct and to measure it before we can use it as a patient reported healthcare outcome.
patient empowerment is a valuable outcome in itself, and is not necessarily contingent on achieving improvements in health status.
the development of a generic measure of empowerment is needed to enable healthcare evaluation based on patient empowerment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patient empowerment is an important outcome from health services, but it needs to be measured in order to be used to evaluate services.
patient empowerment can and should be considered as a valued outcome of healthcare, even when patients do not experience gains in health status.
patient empowerment should be considered as a patient reported health outcome in its own right.
